solve: Fitted by T-2441 to the engraving alone, with the 1911 Sanborn sheet's plan of the main body (trace s20fp-1637-b1: 11.0 m deep, 13.1 m along the front, its south 4.8 m standing 1.0 m forward) as the lengths. The footprint frame's u runs toward the street and its v runs SOUTH on this side of the avenue, so the eye stands north-west of the house, across Prairie Avenue. The engraving's verticals are vertical, so the camera is level, and its principal point's x is taken at the plate's centre (450 px). Four plan corners fix the plan exactly (residual 0 px): the north flank's rear corner at x 92 px, the main front's north corner (behind the swell bay) at x 255 px, the wing's north front corner at x 617 px and its south corner at x 800 px. That gives f = 2967 px, a heading of -64.7 degrees in the footprint frame (looking south-east), the eye 59 m in front of the main front and 23.5 m north of the north wall. A nearer eye cannot hold the four corners on the sheet's plan: freeing the wing's width instead puts its north corner 1.06 m further north than the sheet (f 998 px, the eye 16 m out), and that camera then reads the ground under the bay 2.5 m above the ground under the wing. The draughtsman's perspective is not one camera's, and the plan is the sheet's. Heights at the far camera: the ground at the wing's corner (y 772 px) and under the main corner (775 px), and the cornice's soffit at the wing's corner (262 px), the main corner (262 px) and the flank's rear corner (300 px), least-squares to a horizon at y 573.8 px, the eye 4.44 m over grade and the soffit at 11.34 m, residuals 4-13 px. Read through it: the principal floor about 2.3 m (the wing's balcony floor and the stoop's head, y 668 px), the second floor about 6.6 m, the principal windows 3.0-5.7 m on the wing and 3.0-6.0 m on the bay, the second storey's 7.2-9.5 m, the dormers' sills about 11.5 m and their gables' apexes about 13.5 m, the main roof's level top line 14.1-14.2 m, the stacks' tops 16.4 m (front, x 225 px) and 15.5 m (rear, x 135 px) on the north wall and 14.8 m over the wing. The engraving's cornice lines converge faster than this camera draws them (its front's vanishing point at about x 1850 px, this camera's far to the right), which is the draughtsman's perspective, not the plan's.
